name: Test Coverage Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for test coverage, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for test coverage, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple test coverage strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. When test coverage decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. When test coverage guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Prefer the simplest test coverage approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Keep test coverage changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Before starting test coverage work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Measure before optimizing any test coverage bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Document any non-obvious test coverage decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Prefer explicit, readable test coverage solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Validate test coverage outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen test coverage approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
12. State assumptions about test coverage explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated test coverage concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop test coverage edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting test coverage assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic test coverage advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test coverage correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about test coverage over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
